entries.title: Smaller than a netbook and bigger than a smartphone — net tablets arrive
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010–2011, tens of millions of connected portable devices will likely be purchased by consumers with sore eyes and sore arms. Net tablets, or netTabs, will be based on a new form factor
entries.subject: Tablets
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Part 1).

entries.title: Moore's Law is alive and well in 2010
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010 Moore's Law will probably continue to work just fine.
entries.subject: Moore's Law

entries.title: Cloud computing: more than hype but less than hyper
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010 cloud computing is likely to grow much faster than most other technology verticals but will still fail to reach the heights its more enthusiastic supporters have suggested.
entries.subject: Cloud computing

entries.title: Thinking thin is in again: virtual desktop infrastructures challenge the PC
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010, Virtual Desktop Infrastructure ... will be taken far more seriously than in previous years ... In 2010, over one million seats may go thin client
entries.subject: Virtual desktop infrastructure

entries.title: IT procurement stands on its head
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that 2010 will likely see many enterprise technology and telecommunications purchasing decisions based on the preferences of individual employees, rather than traditional IT department criteria.
entries.subject: Consumerization of IT

entries.title: CleanTech makes a comeback. But solar stays in the shadows
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts mixed performance for the CleanTech sector in 2010. ... The solar technology subsector will likely be outperformed by the broader CleanTech industry.
entries.subject: CleanTech and solar PV

entries.title: From gray to green: technology reinvents cement
entries.quote: Advances in technology may soon lead to the world's first carbon-negative cement plant that could, in the medium term, deliver a significant (at least 5 percent) reduction in global CO2 emissions.
entries.metric: reduction in global CO2 emissions from carbon-negative cement
entries.subject: Low-carbon cement
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication (Part 2). Medium-term horizon, no target year; the text frames benefits over five to 10 years.

entries.title: Linear's got legs: the television and radio schedule stays supreme
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010 most video and audio content will continue to be consumed linearly ... Our estimate is that over 90 percent of all television watched and over 80 percent of all audio content consumed will be via traditional broadcast.
entries.metric: share of TV watched via traditional broadcast
entries.subject: Linear (scheduled) TV viewing

entries.title: The shift to online advertising: more selective, but the trend continues
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010, online advertising spending will not only grow in absolute dollars but is also likely to grow substantially faster than the total advertising market ... from roughly 10 percent at the end of 2009 to 15 percent by the end of 2011.
entries.subject: Online advertising

entries.title: eReaders fill a niche, but eBooks fly off the (virtual) shelves
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010 stand-alone eReader devices will likely sell five million units globally. Meanwhile, electronic versions of books (eBooks) could sell as many as 100 million copies.
entries.subject: E-readers and e-books

entries.title: Publishing fights back: pay walls and micropayments
entries.quote: DTT TMT predicts that in 2010 the newspaper and magazine industry will continue to make noises about charging readers for the online portion of their business. But that talk is unlikely to be matched by actions or results.
entries.subject: News paywalls

entries.title: TV and the Web belong together, but not necessarily on the same screen
entries.quote: By year-end, more than 30 percent of broadband-enabled households are likely to interact occasionally or regularly with what they are watching on television through some form of computing device.
entries.metric: broadband households interacting with TV via a computing device
entries.subject: Second-screen TV viewing

entries.title: Music as a service rises up the charts
entries.quote: In 2010, the number of paying subscribers ... should exceed 10 million for the first time.
entries.subject: Music streaming subscriptions

entries.title: Video-on-demand takes off — thanks to the vending machine
entries.quote: Our expectation is that the volume and value of DVDs distributed via vending machine will double in 2010 ... By the end of 2010, an estimated 30,000 DVD vending machines will be deployed in the US alone
entries.subject: DVD rental kiosks

entries.title: One step back, two steps forward for 3D TV
entries.quote: Following a bumper year for 3D at the movies, DTT TMT anticipates that expectations will be high for an equivalent 3D-fueled boost to the television sector in 2010.
entries.subject: 3D television

notes: 9th edition ('ninth year'). Published as three separate reports: Technology, Media and Telecommunications Predictions 2010. Media: full report PDF (8 predictions). Technology: Parts 1 and 2 of the Mondaq republication read (7 predictions; the full Technology report count is not confirmed). The Telecommunications report was not found (Mondaq article not located; Internet Archive offline at capture). Rank restarts at 1 within each report (section).
